commands.command: Decision 0057: mobile acquisition runtime, workspace registry, and bounded import/export contract
commands.summary: Verified 0057 was free (highest existing decision was 0056) before creating decisions/0057-....md. Settles workspace root/layout, workspace identity (random UUID, never user-influenced), the registry model and its field list (explicitly no credential fields), atomicity/crash-safety (temp-file-then-rename, corrupt-registry fails loudly), concurrency (single active operation via one coordinator), lifecycle states, the staging-then-publish transaction, the SAF native boundary's command shape, persistable-URI-permission policy, the no-broad-storage-permission rule, directory/archive import bounds, path safety (reusing repopact_repository's containment primitives), the symlink policy (reject, never materialize), the duplicate/case-collision comparison rule (fail-closed), cancellation/progress design, export semantics (new-document-or-explicit-replace, never silent overwrite, never automatic write-back), source-divergence detection's honesty requirement (never claim 'unchanged' without evidence), the full typed error taxonomy, the typed command surface, and the future Git seam (acquisition_kind=remote_git and git_state reserved now, no git2/libgit2/gix dependency added).

Added to the Rust workspace (rust/Cargo.toml members + workspace.dependencies). Depends on repopact-repository (for normalize_path/resolve_within_root reuse -- no second, weaker path-containment implementation), serde/serde_json, sha2 (already a workspace dependency), uuid 1.x (v4 feature; already cached locally), and zip 2.4.2 (already cached locally, default-features disabled, deflate feature only). No git2/libgit2/gix dependency was added, per WI065's explicit prohibition.

src/source.rs: a platform-neutral, streaming (never-materializes-the-whole-tree) trait between 'however a tree of bytes was picked' and the bounded Rust importer, satisfying the required mobile-platform-adapter -> AcquisitionSource -> bounded-importer layering. FilesystemSource is the concrete implementation used for desktop-shaped host testing; a future Android SAF bridge implements the same trait against DocumentsContract/DocumentFile instead of repopact-desktop's own code needing to change.

commands.command: Implement bounded directory import (src/import.rs) and archive import/export (src/archive.rs)
commands.summary: Both enforce Decision 0057's bounds (entry count, total bytes, single-file/entry bytes, depth, path length) during traversal/extraction, never only after the fact, and never trust a source/entry-declared size -- actual bytes are always counted by a bounded copy loop that aborts the instant either bound would be exceeded. Both reuse repopact_repository::{normalize_path, resolve_within_root} for containment (src/paths.rs's safe_join), with a documented, tested fix for a real Windows-specific defect this reuse surfaced (see closeout.windows_canonicalization_finding). Both use one CollisionGuard (Unicode-lowercase-folded, per-path-component comparison) to fail closed on exact duplicates, case-only collisions, and file/directory-type collisions -- proven for archives to also require trimming a ZIP directory entry's trailing '/' before it becomes a collision key (a second real defect this work surfaced; see closeout.zip_trailing_slash_finding). Archive import additionally: rejects any entry zip's own enclosed_name() sanitizer refuses (defense in depth on top of this crate's own path-safety gate), rejects symlink entries outright (entry.is_symlink()), and applies a declared-size/compressed-size compression-ratio heuristic before extraction on top of the same runtime byte-counting bound. create_archive always produces a new archive (Decision 0057: never mutates an original in place).

A single JSON document under one native Mutex-guarded coordinator, written only via temp-file-then-fsync-then-atomic-rename (same-directory temp file, so the rename is same-filesystem). A registry that fails to parse is a loud typed error (registry corrupt and was not modified), proven by a test that the corrupt file is left byte-for-byte untouched -- never silently replaced with an empty registry. A dedicated test asserts the serialized WorkspaceRecord never contains a password/token/secret/credential/private_key-named field. clean_stale_registry_temp_files removes orphaned registry.json.tmp-* files at startup without ever touching the published registry.json.

A cooperative CancellationToken (checked between bounded units of work, never inferred from frontend disappearance), a throttled ProgressThrottle (time- and entry-count-gated, so a large import does not emit one event per file), and an OperationCoordinator that rejects a second concurrent acquisition/export operation with a typed ResourceLimit error rather than queuing or interleaving -- proven directly, plus an OperationGuard proving the coordinator releases correctly even through an early return.

Owns the on-disk layout (<root>/registry.json, workspaces/<id>/repository/, workspaces/<id>/local-metadata/, staging/<operation-id>/) and the staging-then-publish transaction: bounded import into staging/<op>/, then create workspaces/<id>/, atomically rename staging/<op>/ into workspaces/<id>/repository/, create local-metadata/, then and only then upsert a ready registry entry. Any import failure or cancellation deletes the staging directory and leaves neither a workspace directory nor a registry entry -- proven directly (failed_import_leaves_no_ready_workspace_and_no_staging_residue), including via a realistic ZIP-based case-collision fixture rather than a Windows-collapsed one. remove_workspace verifies the target is both a registered workspace id and a path actually inside the app-private workspaces root before deleting anything, and is proven never to touch the original import source. A dedicated test simulates a crash mid-import (an orphaned staging/<op>/ left on disk with no registry entry) and proves WorkspaceManager::open cleans the orphan while leaving an already-ready workspace and its registry entry completely intact.

commands.command: repopact_repository::resolve_within_root Windows canonicalization interaction (real finding, documented and fixed, not worked around with a weaker implementation)
commands.summary: resolve_within_root canonicalizes both `root` and `root.join(relative)` independently; on Windows, fs::canonicalize on an *existing* directory (root, which is always created before import) yields an extended-length \\?\-prefixed path, while the same function on the *not-yet-created* destination file (the overwhelmingly common case for every import) falls back to lexical normalization with no such prefix -- so every legitimate join was misreported as escaping the root. Fixed in this crate's own safe_join wrapper (not in repopact-repository, which is out of this work item's touched-file list) by canonicalizing `root` before delegating, documented inline with the exact mechanism, and covered by a regression test.

commands.command: ZIP directory-entry trailing-slash collision-key finding (real finding, fixed)
commands.summary: A ZIP directory entry's name conventionally ends with '/' (zip::read::ZipFile::is_dir() is defined by exactly that convention); using the raw entry name as-is meant a directory entry "thing/" and a file entry "thing" produced different CollisionGuard keys, silently bypassing the required file-vs-directory collision check. Fixed by trimming the trailing '/' before it becomes the collision key or destination path, covered by a regression test (archive::tests::rejects_file_dir_collision).

46/46 passed, covering: normal directory import; normal archive import; '..' traversal, absolute path, drive prefix, UNC prefix, and embedded-NUL path rejection; safe_join containment; symlink-entry rejection (directory import) and archive-symlink rejection; exact-duplicate, case-only, and file/directory-type collision rejection for both directory and archive import (the case-only and file/directory tests use either a real ZIP fixture or a synthetic in-memory AcquisitionSource specifically because this Windows host's own filesystem is case-insensitive and cannot itself hold two colliding real files, which is itself recorded as a real host-environment-specific testing constraint, not a gap in the importer's own logic); entry-count, total-byte, single-file/entry-byte, and depth-bound enforcement (including a test proving a forged/mismatched size hint cannot bypass the runtime byte counter); malformed-ZIP rejection; cancellation for both importers; zip-slip rejection via reject_unsafe_relative_path plus enclosed_name(); a documented proof that the zip crate's own writer already refuses to construct a byte-identical duplicate-filename archive (a real upstream defense-in-depth fact, recorded rather than worked around with a hand-crafted malformed fixture); registry round-trip, corruption-fails-loudly, no-secret-field, and stale-temp-file-cleanup behavior; operation-coordinator single-active-operation and cancellation-token behavior; and the WorkspaceManager-level staging/publish/cleanup/removal/restart-recovery integration tests described above.
